## Swift Package Manager in Flutter

As of the latest release, this feature is now a default: As of the 3.44 release, Flutter uses Swift Package Manager to manage iOS and macOS native dependencies. Flutter continues to support CocoaPods in maintenance mode, however, the CocoaPods registry permanently becomes read-only on December 2, 2026.

As of the 3.44 release, Flutter's Swift Package Manager (SwiftPM) support is on by default. Upgrading Flutter and running your app automatically adds SwiftPM integration. This makes your project download the Swift packages that your Flutter plugins depend on. Importantly, Flutter falls back to CocoaPods for dependencies that don't yet support Swift Package Manager.

## Plugin Validation & Compatibility Errors

The error messages tied to plugin validation (which relates to the `validatePluginSupportsSwiftPackageManager` function) appear in several reported issues. A common error reads: "Plugin 'my_plugin' is only Swift Package Manager compatible. Try enabling Swift Package Manager by running 'flutter config --enable-swift-package-manager' or remove the plugin as a dependency."

This validation behavior has caused problems in some scenarios — for example, when trying to resolve iOS dependencies on a non-macOS machine. There's also a reported issue where building or running flutter pub commands produces the error that a plugin is only Swift Package Manager compatible, and running flutter config --enable-swift-package-manager doesn't resolve it.

For plugin authors, the guidance around dependency management (relevant to the `darwin_dependency_management` concept) is that plugins should maintain dual support: This guide shows how to add Swift Package Manager support to a plugin that already supports CocoaPods. This ensures the plugin is usable by all Flutter projects. Flutter plugins should support both Swift Package Manager and CocoaPods until further notice.

The reason for maintaining both is a transitional compatibility concern: Swift Package Manager adoption will be gradual. As of Flutter 3.44, plugins that don't support CocoaPods aren't usable by projects that haven't migrated to Swift Package Manager yet. Plugins that don't support Swift Package Manager can cause problems for projects that have migrated.

## The Shared Darwin Directory

The `darwin` reference in your query also relates to Flutter's shared source concept: When sharedDarwinSource is enabled, instead of an ios directory for iOS and a macos directory for macOS, both platforms use a shared darwin directory for all code and resources. When adding SwiftPM support, plugin authors are told the example uses ios, but to replace ios with macos or darwin, as applicable.
